summary: EASD 2026 (Milan, 28 Sept–2 Oct) is driving GLP-1 news this week. Over the next 3–10 days, most new GLP-1 search demand will probably come from conference data: the pancreatic cancer safety study, CagriSema vs tirzepatide, retatrutide, orforglipron by menopause stage, and the tirzepatide switch/heart data. Our biggest openings, in order: (1) the regulator-required Nordic semaglutide pancreatic cancer study (97,464 users, HR 0.91). It's brand new, reassuring and myth-busting, with a concrete number. (2) The WashU/VA study (333k veterans) on stopping GLP-1s and heart risk. It fits the "keeping results" pillar. The framing must be "talk to your prescriber before any change", never stopping advice. (3) Hair shedding on GLP-1s. The Guardian, a Clin Dermatol review and the Times of India all ran it, so search demand is high, and our protein angle is helpful. (4) GLP-1 vs CPAP for sleep apnea (JAMA Otolaryngology review). (5) The STEP UP MRI analysis of muscle quality. Carry-overs still worth making: the SELECT mediation study (~20% of the heart benefit explained by weight loss) and the tirzepatide brown-fat study (mice only). Rejected: GLP-1 microdosing, which is trending in Oprah Daily and mindbodygreen but is a banned topic. We list it only so downstream agents know to avoid it. Handle with caution: the NAION/vision-loss lawsuits and GLP-1 prescribing without an approved indication.

candidates.topic: Regulator-required Nordic study: no link between semaglutide and pancreatic cancer (97,464 users, HR 0.91, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does Ozempic cause pancreatic cancer?' A myth-bust with one concrete number: across Denmark, Sweden and Norway, 97,464 semaglutide users showed no raised risk vs other diabetes drugs (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.71–1.16). Say plainly that follow-up is short (under 2 years after a 1-year lag), that this was an EASD conference presentation and not yet a full paper as of late Sept 2026, and that the population was adults with type 2 diabetes compared with sulfonylureas, SGLT2 inhibitors or insulin.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD Milan on Sept 28, with Medscape and Medical Xpress coverage the same evening. Almost no creator videos yet. Cancer worry is one of the top safety searches among GLP-1 users, and this answers it with a reassuring, regulator-mandated study.

evidence.signal: Regulator-mandated active-comparator cohort in 3 Nordic registries; 97,464 semaglutide users; pooled HR 0.91 (0.71–1.16); no dose-response; limitation: short follow-up
'Semaglutide Not Linked to Higher Pancreatic Cancer Risk', Sept 28

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1 medicines linked to up to 22% higher heart attack, stroke and death risk at 2 years (WashU, 333,000+ US veterans with type 2 diabetes)
candidates.angle: 'The heart benefit builds slowly and fades fast': why GLP-1 treatment is usually thought of as long-term, and what questions to take to your prescriber if cost, side effects or supply make you consider a break. Say it's observational (an association, not proof of cause) and that the population was veterans with type 2 diabetes. No stopping or switching advice. The message is 'talk to your prescriber before any change'.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
do you have to take ozempic forever
candidates.why_now: The ScienceDaily release came out around Sept 20, and the Scripps local-TV syndication hit dozens of stations on Sept 28. Separately, the Glasgow Live 'flu-like symptom when stopping' story shows UK demand. 'Can I stop?' is a big evergreen question, and this gives it a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: 333k veterans with T2D; 6+ month interruption tied to higher MACE; up to 22% higher risk at 2 years; benefits not fully restored on restart
Press release, Sept 2026
Syndicated national coverage, Sept 28

candidates.topic: GLP-1 hair shedding: what the 2026 reviews show, why it happens (telogen effluvium after rapid weight loss) and how protein and nutrition may help
candidates.angle: 'Is my hair falling out because of Ozempic?' Explain that the shedding reported with GLP-1s looks mostly like temporary telogen effluvium tied to rapid weight loss, not direct damage to hair follicles, that it usually recovers, and the evidence-based basics: enough protein, check iron, B12 and vitamin D with your clinician, and don't crash-diet on top of the medicine. Keep the stronger tirzepatide signal worded as 'reported more often'.
keywords: hair loss on zepbound how to stop
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (Sept 27), Times of India (Sept 28) and a new Clin Dermatol review (Sept 21) all landed together. The search demand is huge and persistent, and most existing videos are selling supplements, so an evidence-based, reassuring take stands out.

evidence.signal: 'Hair and Scalp Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Practice', Sept 21, 2026
GLP-1 therapies and hair loss: systematic review and counseling implications
'Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?', Sept 27

candidates.topic: CagriSema beat tirzepatide 5 mg on weight (12.4% vs 9.1%) in type 2 diabetes: REIMAGINE 5, with the lowest-dose caveat
candidates.angle: 'Headlines say Novo's new drug beat Mounjaro. Here's the fine print.' CagriSema 1.0/1.0 mg vs tirzepatide 5 mg (the starting maintenance dose, which can go up to 15 mg) over 68 weeks in about 1,000 adults with T2D. HbA1c results were similar (−1.71 vs −1.67 points, non-inferior). Explain amylin plus GLP-1 in simple terms. The trial was open-label, the results are top-line only, and the FDA decision on CagriSema for weight management is expected Q4 2026.
candidates.why_now: Top-line results came out Sept 21, then Pharmacy Times on Sept 28, NewsNation calling it 'outperforms Zepbound', and heavy finance coverage. EASD presentations keep it in the news, and the FDA decision is coming in Q4.

evidence.signal: REIMAGINE 5 top-line: 12.4% vs 9.1% weight loss; HbA1c non-inferior
'CagriSema Tops Tirzepatide 5 mg', Sept 28
NCT06221969 registry, open-label, T2D on metformin ± SGLT2i

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and sleep apnea: 6–22 fewer breathing events per hour vs about 31 with CPAP (JAMA Otolaryngology review)
candidates.angle: 'Can a GLP-1 replace your CPAP?' The positive, accurate answer: GLP-1s, especially tirzepatide (FDA-approved as Zepbound for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity), reduce apnea events, partly by shrinking tongue fat. CPAP still does more, and the two can work together. Remind viewers not to stop CPAP without talking to their sleep doctor.
candidates.why_now: The Nexstar syndication ('CPAP remains best treatment') ran on dozens of local stations from Sept 26–28, plus Yahoo Health ('Should you take a GLP-1 for OSA?') and bioengineer.org. It's a benefits-beyond-weight pillar with a very concrete comparison.

evidence.signal: JAMA Otolaryngology review: 6–22 fewer AHI events/hr vs ~31 for CPAP; tongue fat reduction
GLP-1 RAs in OSA: cardiometabolic and respiratory outcomes
Precision pharmacotherapy for OSA review

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) pill: similar weight loss (up to ~14%) in pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women (ATTAIN-1/ATTAIN-2 post hoc, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause stop GLP-1s from working?' This analysis suggests the effect is similar across menopausal stages. Use it to explain the daily pill with no food or water rules, and name the limits: post hoc, some subgroups as small as 10, Lilly-funded. Cite ATTAIN-1 (no diabetes) and ATTAIN-2 (T2D) correctly for each number.
candidates.why_now: EASD presentation, with News-Medical and Medical Xpress coverage Sept 26–28 and Everyday Health's 'Can GLP-1s benefit women in menopause?' on Sept 28. Menopause is one of the hottest women's health themes, and it's in our snapshots too (HRT and blood clots).

evidence.signal: Similar weight loss across three menopausal stages
Up to 14% weight reduction at every menopause stage
Post hoc subgroup analysis ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2

candidates.topic: STEP UP MRI: what semaglutide 7.2 mg does to thigh muscle volume, fat inside muscle and physical function
candidates.angle: 'Muscle loss on GLP-1: quantity vs quality.' Use the new MRI secondary analysis to explain lean-mass loss alongside less fat inside the muscle, and why function matters more than a DEXA number. Pair it with the evidence-based fixes: protein and strength training. Check the exact effect sizes in the paper before scripting.
keywords: how to keep muscle on wegovy
candidates.why_now: Published Sept 20 in Diabetes Obes Metab with almost no press yet. Muscle loss is a top-3 GLP-1 worry. A Clin Nutr creatine commentary (Sept 21) and a Nutritional Outlook piece (Sept 28) show the topic is heating up in both industry and research.

evidence.signal: STEP UP secondary analysis: thigh muscle volume, fat infiltration, physical function
STEP UP registry NCT05646706
Lean mass preservation in GLP-1 treatment: nutrition, exercise, monitoring

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation, European Heart Journal) plus what predicted who lost the most in SELECT (Diabetes Care)
candidates.angle: 'Your heart may benefit even if the scale moves slowly.' Keep the population exact (adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight/obesity, no diabetes) and note that the rest of the benefit is still unexplained (News-Medical: 'researchers still cannot fully explain why').
keywords: ozempic heart benefit not weight loss
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots with steady momentum of about 72. News-Medical coverage came Sept 28, and the Diabetes Care predictors paper came Sept 24. It still has little creator coverage.

evidence.signal: SELECT mediation analysis, Sept 23
Predictors of peak body weight loss in SELECT
'Semaglutide cuts major heart events, but researchers still cannot fully explain why'

candidates.topic: Retatrutide, the 'triple hormone' shot: up to 28.3% weight loss (TRIUMPH-1) and new diabetes data at EASD 2026
candidates.angle: 'What's a triple agonist and why is everyone talking about it?' Explain GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon simply, give the phase 3 numbers with the right populations (TRIUMPH-1: 2,339 adults with obesity and no diabetes, up to 28.3% over 80 weeks vs 2.2% placebo; TRANSCEND-T2D-1: up to 15.3%), and stress that it's investigational and not approved. Firmly warn against gray-market 'research' retatrutide, since the Philippine FDA issued a warning Sept 26.
candidates.why_now: New T2D data opened EASD (Medical Daily, Sept 28). Search interest in retatrutide keeps climbing, fuelled partly by gray-market peptide hype, so a trustworthy explainer that sends people away from illegal sources is valuable.

evidence.signal: TRANSCEND-T2D-1 and TRIUMPH-1 phase 3 results
Lilly to present Foundayo, retatrutide, eloraTZP data at EASD 2026
Retatrutide diabetes results lead EASD 2026 opening

candidates.topic: GLP-1 stigma: users hide their medicine from friends and family, and even from doctors (FSU interview study, Health Communication)
candidates.angle: 'Taking a GLP-1 isn't the easy way out.' Explain obesity as a chronic disease, what the medicine does biologically, and the 'weight bias paradox'. It's a warm, community-building piece. Be clear it's a qualitative study of 34 adults (themes, not prevalence).
keywords: should I tell people I'm on ozempic
candidates.why_now: Newsweek (Sept 28) and the FSU release (Sept 24), plus the Seattle Times on GLP-1 support communities and the STAT 'lifestyle drug' debate. It fits our compassion mission and is highly shareable.

evidence.signal: 34-adult interview study, Health Communication, Sept 2026
'GLP-1 Users Face Stigma From Friends and Family'

candidates.topic: Why GLP-1s work less well for some people: up to ~15% see limited weight loss, and what trials say about 'responders'
candidates.angle: 'Not losing much on Mounjaro or Wegovy? You're not broken.' Use STEP/SURMOUNT responder rates (e.g. share reaching ≥5%), the SELECT predictors paper, and the fact that benefits beyond weight still count. Send people to their prescriber rather than suggesting any dose changes.
keywords: why am I not losing weight on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: DongA Science (Sept 27) on 'limited effect in up to 15%', plus the Diabetes Care SELECT predictors paper and real-world tirzepatide cohort papers this week. 'Not working' is a huge query with poor-quality answers out there.

evidence.signal: Predictors of peak body weight loss with semaglutide in SELECT
Limited effect in up to 15% of patients
Tirzepatide long-term real-world effectiveness systematic review

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide switched on calorie-burning brown fat, but only in obese mice
candidates.angle: 'Does Mounjaro speed up your metabolism?' A clear 'mouse study, not a human result' explainer that uses it to teach how GLP-1/GIP act on appetite vs energy use. The payoff is honest: in humans, appetite reduction explains most of the effect.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily (Sept 26), Yahoo and Health and Me (Sept 27–28), and our snapshots jumped from 58 to 76. Headlines oversell it, so a myth-bust fits our playbook.

evidence.signal: 'Zepbound and Mounjaro may turn on the body's calorie-burning brown fat'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 and dementia: EVOKE trials didn't slow early Alzheimer's, but diabetes-cohort data still show lower progression from MCI
candidates.angle: 'Can Ozempic protect your brain?' Balanced: the randomized EVOKE/EVOKE+ trials in early Alzheimer's did not show slowing, while observational target-trial emulations in people with T2D and MCI show an association. Explain why RCTs outrank cohorts, in a positive, curious tone.
candidates.why_now: J Prev Alzheimers Dis EVOKE lessons (Sept 24) and Alzheimers Dement TRCI target-trial (Sept 20). Brain-health curiosity is high. Verify EVOKE outcomes carefully before scripting.

evidence.signal: EVOKE(+) semaglutide in early Alzheimer's: lessons and implications
Dementia progression with GLP-1 RAs in MCI + T2D: target-trial emulation

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF): new meta-analyses of tirzepatide and semaglutide
candidates.angle: 'The breathless, swollen-ankle kind of heart failure': explain HFpEF with obesity and what STEP-HFpEF/SUMMIT-based meta-analyses show on symptoms and events, naming the exact population.
candidates.why_now: Drugs meta-analysis (Sept 26), NMCD meta-analysis (Sept 8), JACC Case Rep (Sept 25) and J Arrhythm on AF in HFpEF. A cluster of papers but little consumer coverage, so we'd be early.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs in heart failure: phenotype-specific meta-analysis
Tirzepatide and semaglutide in HFpEF with obesity: meta-analysis

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and periods: reported changes in bleeding and ovulation, and the fertility/contraception point
candidates.angle: 'Why your cycle may change on a GLP-1': weight loss can restore ovulation (relevant in PCOS), so pregnancy is possible, and there are reports of bleeding changes. Give general guidance to discuss contraception and pregnancy plans with a prescriber. Check the underlying study quality before scripting.
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Health (Sept 26) and mindbodygreen on GLP-1 after menopause. Women are a large share of our audience, and competition from evidence-based sources is low.

evidence.signal: 'Semaglutide was linked to changes in women's periods — including heavy bleeding and missed ovulation'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 vision-loss (NAION) lawsuits: what the evidence says about the eye risk
candidates.angle: A calm, factual explainer: what NAION is, what regulators (EMA listed it as a very rare side effect of semaglutide) and studies show, symptoms that need urgent care, and why to tell your eye doctor you're on a GLP-1. No legal or fear framing. Verify the current EMA/FDA label wording before scripting.
candidates.why_now: Boston.com, MassLive and NewsNation lawsuit stories from Sept 26–28. Search spikes are driven by fear, so a trustworthy explainer adds value, but it needs a careful tone.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 companies face flurry of lawsuits after consumers say drugs caused vision loss'

candidates.topic: GLP-1 'microdosing' trend (Oprah Daily, mindbodygreen, Yahoo Creators)
candidates.angle: Do not produce. Microdosing and self-titration protocols are on the brand's never-cover list and push people toward compounded or gray-market sources. At most, downstream agents can say 'dosing decisions belong with your prescriber' inside other pieces.
candidates.why_now: Several lifestyle outlets pushed it Sept 27–28, but it's banned by the brand guardrails.

evidence.signal: 'Microdosing GLP-1s Promises Weight Loss with Minimal Side Effects'
